claims.claim: Theoretical state space duality (SSD) framework connecting SSMs and attention variants via semiseparable matrices
claims.quote: develop a rich framework of theoretical connections between SSMs and variants of attention, connected through various decompositions of a well-studied class of structured semiseparable matrices

claims.claim: Generalization of linear attention to structured masked attention (SMA)
claims.quote: and then generalize it to a new family of structured masked attention (SMA)

claims.claim: Proof that any kernel attention with a fast recurrent form must be an SSM
claims.quote: We also prove that any kernel attention method possessing a fast recurrent form must be an SSM.

claims.claim: New hardware-efficient SSD algorithm, faster than Mamba scan and competitive with FlashAttention-2
claims.quote: SSD is highly competitive with optimized implementations of softmax attention (FlashAttention-2 (Dao 2024)), crossing over at sequence length 2K and 6× faster at sequence length 16K.

claims.claim: Introduce heads from multi-head attention to SSMs (head structure design, MVA/MIS pattern)
claims.quote: For example, we introduce the analog of heads from multi-head attention (MHA) to SSMs.
claims.ablation_quote: Table 5 ablates choices of the multi-head structure for the Mamba-2 architecture.

claims.claim: Modified Mamba block with grouped-value head structure and parallel data-dependent projections at block start
claims.quote: The main ideas include introducing grouped-value attention (GVA) head structure, and moving all data-dependent projections to occur in parallel at the beginning of the block.
claims.ablation_quote: Table 4 ablates these architecture changes to the block, which occur outside of the core SSM layer.

claims.claim: Mamba-2 architecture combining parallel block with SSD as inner SSM layer
claims.quote: The combination of the modified parallel Mamba block, together with using SSD as the inner SSM layer, results in the Mamba-2 architecture.
claims.ablation_quote: Surprisingly, it is significantly better than Mamba-1 even when the state sizes are controlled (N = 16).

claims.claim: Mamba-2 Pareto dominates Mamba and Transformer++ in Chinchilla scaling laws
claims.quote: finding that it Pareto dominates Mamba and Transformer++ in both perplexity and wall-clock time

claims.claim: Mamba-2 2.7B outperforms Mamba-2.8B, Pythia-2.8B and Pythia-6.9B on downstream evaluations
claims.quote: Mamba-2 with 2.7B parameters trained on 300B tokens on the Pile outperforms Mamba-2.8B, Pythia-2.8B and even Pythia-6.9B trained on the same dataset.

claims.claim: Tensor-parallel-friendly design halving synchronization points per block
claims.quote: We design Mamba-2 to be TP-friendly, reducing the number of synchronization point per block by half.

claims.claim: Sequence parallelism for SSMs by passing recurrent states between devices
claims.quote: We describe how to train SSMs in general and Mamba-2 in particular with sequence parallelism, by passing the recurrent states between devices.

claims.claim: Efficient variable-length training without padding tokens
claims.quote: We show how Mamba-2 can be trained with variable sequence lengths efficiently, requiring no padding tokens.

data_disclosure.quote: we train Mamba-2 on 300B tokens on the Pile, using the GPT-NeoX (Black et al. 2022) tokenizer.

tokens_disclosed.quote: we train Mamba-2 on 300B tokens on the Pile, using the GPT-NeoX (Black et al. 2022) tokenizer.

coding.note: Mainly an architecture and theory paper, but it trains Mamba-2 models and releases the checkpoints, so I coded it as a release report. Ablation calls: Table 4 compares parallel vs sequential projections and Table 5 compares head patterns. Both use a similar parameter count and token budget, so both are coded YES. For the SSD layer replacing S6, the only comparison is Mamba-1 vs Mamba-2 on MQAR with matched state size, and the whole block differs, so it is coded PARTIAL. The paper never says whether comparator scores were re-run or copied (they likely come from the Mamba paper), so both fields are NR. Data is coded FULL because all pre-training is on the Pile alone, a single public dataset. A stricter reading would make this PARTIAL. Comparators are drawn from Table 1, which is extended by Table 10, plus Transformer++ from the scaling and hybrid comparisons. No compute (GPU-hours or FLOPs) is reported.
